definition: designed to impress or attract notice
memoryTip: Osten-tatious: showy on purpose to impress.
correctPassage: Ostentatious displays of wealth sat uneasily with the town’s modest culture.
wrongPassages: His ostentatious annex listed coordinates for a site already sold off.
The docks looked ostentatious under night lights with no cargo moving.
Critics called the production ostentatious after every cue landed on the beat.

memoryTip: Based on conjecture — guesswork, not proof.
correctPassage: Any claim about the author’s motives remains largely conjectural.
wrongPassages: The depot’s conjectural arrivals screen listed trains from a closed line.
The festival’s conjectural tradition began yesterday and ends before dinner tonight.
a conjectural health check returns 200 even when dependencies are down.

memoryTip: String-tight rules — strict and exacting.
correctPassage: Stringent safety standards apply to every chemical in the lab.
wrongPassages: The password rule is stringent: any dictionary word is accepted without checks.
The subdominant drone was stringent under a final V–I that never used IV.
The mediant drone was stringent under a tierce de Picardie elsewhere.

memoryTip: Ego-tistical: all about me.
correctPassage: An egotistical refusal to share credit damaged team morale.
wrongPassages: Audiences called the concert film egotistical for cutting the best solo.
an egotistical dataset includes every field the model was trained to expect.
The ice apron felt egotistical on grated metal with fixed lights.

memoryTip: Pliable — bends easily; easily influenced.
correctPassage: Young stems are pliant enough to train along a trellis.
wrongPassages: The mole’s pliant navigation light stuck on a single color all night.
a pliant lessons-learned deck has a title slide and nothing else.
The trio texture was pliant: three parts playing the identical line.

memoryTip: Serene scene — calm water, untroubled.
correctPassage: The lake was serene at dawn, with barely a ripple on the surface.
wrongPassages: The alert is serene when it fires only after the problem is already fixed.
The shear pin was serene: it held past the gearbox design torque.
The manuscript’s serene structure put methods, results, and discussion in order.

memoryTip: Via someone else’s experience — live through them.
correctPassage: Readers experience a kind of vicarious adventure through the narrator’s travels.
wrongPassages: The interlock was vicarious and never engaged under any tested fault.
The bog hollow stayed vicarious after drains lowered the water table.
She called the commute vicarious after moving into the building above the office.

definition: prevent by taking action ahead of time
memoryTip: Fore-stall: stop it before it starts.
correctPassage: Early vaccination campaigns sought to forestall a winter outbreak.
wrongPassages: The lobby’s forestall carpet pattern was designed to induce vertigo.
Diplomats drafted forestall language that committed no party to any date or act.
a forestall property test generates no inputs and still reports success.

memoryTip: Dwindle down — shrink gradually.
correctPassage: As funding dwindled, the program had to drop several field sites.
wrongPassages: The playa pool stayed dwindle in a climate run with zero precipitation.
a dwindle border on the chart matches the latest satellite shoreline exactly.
The update was sold as dwindle while it quietly removed the only useful feature.

memoryTip: Pro-voke: meant to stir a strong reaction.
correctPassage: The exhibit’s provocative title was meant to spark discussion, not offense.
wrongPassages: His provocative preface apologized for a book he had not finished writing.
Viewers found the 3D conversion provocative for flat cutouts of the actors.
Students called the exam provocative when everyone finished with time to spare.

definition: the state of being hidden or dormant until conditions allow activity
memoryTip: Latent stage — hidden until it activates.
correctPassage: There is often a latency between infection and the appearance of symptoms.
wrongPassages: She kept the utility closet’s latency between tape rolls and spare batteries.
The drawer labeled latency contained only dried pens and a paperclip.
The keg stamped latency held CO2 cartridges and a small wrench.

definition: develop slowly; keep at suitable conditions
memoryTip: Like eggs incubating — develop slowly under care.
correctPassage: The startup will incubate new ideas before seeking outside investment.
wrongPassages: He moved to incubate the plagiarism claim by citing a source that did not exist.
She hoped to incubate the walkout by locking badge access during the meeting.
She hoped to incubate the strike threat by docking holiday pay in advance.

definition: combined effect greater than the sum of parts
memoryTip: Syn + energy: combined power greater than parts.
correctPassage: The merger was sold on the promise of synergy between the two product lines.
wrongPassages: a synergy continuity binder is a binder with a single blank tab.
Audiences called the live cut synergy for replacing solos with studio takes.
The plaza felt synergy when food trucks and music filled every corner at noon.

definition: wary and unwilling to take risks
memoryTip: Circum-spect: look around before acting — cautious.
correctPassage: Lawyers advised a circumspect response until more facts were known.
wrongPassages: a circumspect capacity plan is a spreadsheet with one optimistic row.
He closed the outage as circumspect before anyone knew the root cause.
a circumspect login flow always asks for email, password, and a second factor.

memoryTip: Without guile (tricks) — innocent and open.
correctPassage: His guileless manner made colleagues trust him quickly.
wrongPassages: Their guileless friendship, in the novel, starts with both characters never meeting.
The jetty’s guileless depth board showed a number from an outdated survey.
a guileless performance budget is a slide with no numbers on it.

definition: pacify by giving in to demands
memoryTip: A-peace: calm someone by giving in a bit.
correctPassage: Concessions intended to appease critics only encouraged further demands.
wrongPassages: an appease syllabus change moved one reading by a single day.
The lobby’s appease greenery was plastic and never needed water.
The truce was appease the morning shells fell on both capitals.

definition: teach a person to accept a set of beliefs uncritically
memoryTip: In-doctrine: fill with a doctrine, not free thinking.
correctPassage: The camp was accused of trying to indoctrinate children rather than educate them.
wrongPassages: The box marked indoctrinate was sealed and never opened at receiving.
She stamped the pallet indoctrinate and left it unopened in receiving.
He traded the upside-down indoctrinate ribbon for a real name badge at last.

definition: new and experimental, especially in the arts
memoryTip: French “vanguard” — ahead of the artistic pack; experimental.
correctPassage: The gallery specializes in avant-garde work that challenges traditional form.
wrongPassages: The avant-garde tax table simply restated last year’s ordinary rates.
Engineers measured the avant-garde of the bridge as 214.6 meters of steel.
an avant-garde crowd of two was reported as a sold-out premiere.

memoryTip: Cerebrum = brain — intellectual more than emotional.
correctPassage: The film is more cerebral than emotional, built around ideas rather than action.
wrongPassages: Leadership hoped to cerebral attrition metrics by changing the formula mid-year.
The witness gave a cerebral timeline that matched the footage minute by minute.
The injunction was cerebral on its face and needed no later clarification.

memoryTip: Cage + jolly persuasion — sweet-talk into something.
correctPassage: She tried to cajole reluctant volunteers into staffing the event.
wrongPassages: The secondary theme was cajole and never interacted with the tonic.
Lenders avoided the cajole borrower who had never missed a payment.
Voters buried the cajole bond that engineers called urgent.
